## The traps, in the order they will bite you

- **Ordering is behaviour** (risk 5). Body parse, then the two rate limits — spent *before* `invalid_token`, deliberately — then the licence seat, then the flag wall; then the sweep kick. Reordering any of it changes a status code or a 429 budget. `authorize` returns `Promise<Response | Caller>` and its `return fail(…)` lines stay exactly as they are; the caller checks `instanceof Response`.
- **Deno resolution** (risk 1). Relative specifiers carry the `.ts` extension. Files stay flat, so every `../_shared/x.mjs` specifier is byte-unchanged. `import type` for `Caller` and `Sql` — a value import of a type-only module is a real module edge. Do not add a `deno.json` or an import map; none exists under `server/`, and the CLI would pick a per-function one up and change how this function resolves.
- **What actually deploys** (risk 2). `--use-api` uploads the import graph from `index.ts`, not the directory, while `supabase functions serve` mounts the whole directory — so a module reached only dynamically works locally and is *missing in production*. Static imports only, checked with 8a.3. No new file may be named `index.ts`.
- **Module-load side effects** (risk 3). `bucket.ts` reads the R2 env and prints the boot line when it is evaluated. ESM evaluates a module once per isolate however many files import it, so the line still prints exactly once — verify that in your own serve log rather than assuming it. Never copy that block into a second module, never import `bucket.ts` from outside `collab/` (`account/` has its own line on purpose), and only `index.ts` may call `Deno.serve`.
- **The shared-rule hazard** (risk 9). Every predicate stays imported from `_shared/collab.mjs`. Do not copy a rule into a new home to save an import.
